name: The Welcome Bath
pitch: A Qi Refining bath attendant washes your layers off and wears them: she beats the top-end in 2 seconds and takes 4 to beat an ordinary person.
power: legend against the rich, ordinary against the poor

new.name: Wash the Dust
new.effect: A cleanse aimed at the target. Closes your own L2 to L5.

new.name: Washing
new.effect: An art with the wash tag zeroes the target's largest of L2 to L5 for the fight, and you add 50 % of it to the same layer. L1 never washes.

new.name: Towel Only
new.effect: Your own L2 to L5 count for nothing.
new.second_home: any build that lives on borrowed layers

new.name: Both Hands
new.effect: The first firing of a fight takes two layers.

new.name: Down to the Skin
new.effect: With no layer left, a wash takes 40 ward strength and efficiency, and you keep your share.

new.name: Attendant's Manual
new.effect: Main, tier 1, names Water, no bonuses, gives three arts.

new.name: Wash the Dust
new.effect: Body, cleanse, wash, c_art 1.3, cost 0.04, 0.5 s.

questions: Rule 2 gives this to NPCs. A generated attendant strips a player's whole stack. Should status resistance or a realm gap bound the share?
The top-end anchors sit in L2 to L5, so one wash art inverts the ladder. Is a build meant to be a hard counter to being rich?
Who opens a fight decided this build until Both Hands. Is rule 10's requesting side meant to matter that much?
